biggest_catch: Ubertesters' official pages say testers are 'rewarded per testing hour' but publish no actual hourly rate — you cannot know what a study pays before doing it.
catches: Official pages say testers are rewarded per testing hour, with the rate varying by level, experience, location, and project complexity — no concrete number is published.
The professional QA route requires certification plus theory and practical tests (unpaid entry work) before paid access.
Payment is typically made no later than the end of the following month — slow payout timing.
No current official pay figure exists to anchor the route's earnings claim.

c1.evidence: Ubertesters is a real operating company; the content lives on the official ubertesters.com domain.

c2.evidence: Official become-a-tester and community pages exist but publish no concrete pay rate — only that testers are 'rewarded per testing hour' at varying rates.

c3.evidence: No upfront fee to join; certification/theory/practical tests are unpaid entry work, not a fee.

c4.evidence: No concrete current official pay figure on the Ubertesters domain.

eligibility: Sign up as a tester; the professional QA route requires certification and passing theory/practical tests. No official pay-linked eligibility terms published.
